paper_id: Automating Release of Deep Link APIs for Android Applications
title: Automating Release of Deep Link APIs for Android Applications
motivation: 73% of top Android apps lack deep links; developers need 45–411 LoC manual changes per deep link, hindering web-like mobile experience
problem_framing: Automate deep-link release by combining static analysis (navigation graphs) and dynamic analysis (fragment identification) with minimal developer effort
key_insight: Cooperative static-dynamic analysis plus deep-link proxy enables reaching arbitrary app locations without modifying business logic
method_signature: Navigation graph + shortest-path analysis + UI-tree fragment ID + deep-link proxy replay engine
evaluation_criteria: Coverage increase percentage across 20 apps; runtime overhead marginality
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Objects of app-specific classes in intents cannot be populated; static analysis cannot analyze dynamic fragments; low coverage of dynamic analysis
evidence_for_taste: only about 35% of apps have deep links
73% of the top 20,000 apps do not have deep links
static analysis cannot reach the dynamic contents
no interference of the normal functionalities
thinking_moves: 从20,000 app大规模实测归纳覆盖率低的客观现象
用GitHub commit history量化开发者手动改写成本(45-411 LoC)
把深链接问题拆解为activity路径和fragment状态两步
静态分析确定最短activity跳转序列, 动态分析补足fragment级状态
proxy架构规避对原业务逻辑的侵入
